name: Socket outlet with interlocked switch
summary: Plan mark for an outlet whose switch is mechanically interlocked so a plug cannot be inserted or withdrawn while live.
description: Interlocked socket outlets are used for industrial plugs, welding outlets, portable plant supplies and higher-current three-phase outlets. The interlock forces the user to switch off before the plug can be removed or inserted, which prevents drawing an arc at the pins. The plan mark adds a switch stroke and a small interlock bar to the outlet form.

On industrial layouts the symbol is often paired with a current rating and pole count written beside it, for example 32 A 5-pin. The estimator should expect a heavier enclosure, sometimes with an integral fuse or circuit breaker, and the installer should expect a surface-mounted accessory rather than a flush plate.
The interlock mark does not confirm the presence of overcurrent or residual-current protection inside the unit. Check the schedule for combination units that include a breaker or RCD.
readingNotes: Check the rating text: interlocked outlets are usually specified by current, poles and IP rating together.
Do not confuse the interlock bar with the protective earth bar on a domestic outlet.
drawingChecklist: State current rating, pole count and plug standard.
State whether overcurrent or residual-current protection is integral.
Note IP rating and mounting surface.
distinction: A simple switched outlet allows the plug to be withdrawn while energised; the interlocked form mechanically prevents it.
